Read for a regression this change could have introduced and did not: now that retro's deletion-only head has check runs of its own, packages/daemon/internal/api/ready.go:173-184 refuses a required check only when its result is Missing or red and returns nil while it is still running, so READY at a fresh retro head whose checks are in flight is accepted; packages/daemon/internal/classify/decisions.go:29 and :144-153 use the handoff-only classification only to decide whether a red counts a fix attempt, never to suppress reading a red, and SettlementFor (decisions.go:59-76) records a settlement for the current head itself, so retro's head's own verdict replaces the carried one. Neither file is touched by this change.

The reviewer's recorded risk - READY reaching a retro head in the seconds before GitHub has created its check runs, where ready.go would answer READY_CHECKS_NOT_GREEN with 'its push may have skipped CI' - is now bounded from one real measurement rather than left open. This round's code commit 280e1a2d was made at 17:01:51Z (jj committer timestamp) and GitHub created all five workflow runs for it at 17:02:17Z, so the check runs existed within 26 s of the commit and less than that after the push, which happened between the two. My round-one cure proof agrees loosely: runs were present on the cured head at the first read, 70 s after the push. What stays unmeasured is the live interval between retro's push and the merger's first READY read, which no surface here can drive: it spans the daemon observing retro's completion, moving the phase, starting the merger's container, and the merger's own several GitHub reads, all of which plausibly exceed that window - and a READY refusal records nothing, so the merger's next call at the same commit is applied. The risk is real but small and self-clearing, and it is not introduced by this change: it is the shape every retro that writes a learning has always had.

The lock the reviewer asked for landed in one place, packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts, and my round-one note that it was missing is answered. My earlier message to the architect said the lock needed two assertions in two suites because @legion/pi-shared's skills-guard helpers stage only skills/; that is true of the helpers but not of the test file, which reads packages/daemon/internal/prompts directly through its own promptsRoot at line 24. One test covering all four files is the better answer, and the mutation matrix above confirms it covers them.
